root.name: Benoni Defense: Mikenas Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 c5 3. d5 e6 4. Nc3 exd5 5. cxd5 d6 6. e4 g6 7. f4 Bg7 8. e5

overview: In the Four Pawns Attack White plays 8.e5, charging the centre. Black meets it with 8...dxe5 9.fxe5 Nfd7 or 8...Nfd7 9.Nb5, and the position becomes sharp with big tactics on d6, e6 and f7. Both sides need to know the forcing lines.

white_ideas.idea: Break with e5 and e6 to attack f7
Use Nb5-d6+ to disrupt the position

black_ideas.idea: Take on e5 and win material or defend precisely
Counter on the long diagonal with ...Bg7

typical_structures.structure: Four Pawns centre with c4, d5, e5, f4

character.notes: A highly forcing and theoretical line.

gambit.notes: Material is level in the main line since the e-pawn is recaptured.

structure.notes: A sharp central break in an asymmetric centre.

character.reason: White pushes in the centre and both sides face forcing tactics.

gambit.reason: Material is level in the main lines as the e5 pawn is recaptured.

soundness.reason: Heavily analysed, and both sides have a path.

structure.reason: An asymmetric Benoni centre with the e-file opening.

level.reason: The forcing lines must be known.

plans.reason: White uses the pawn mass to attack f7 and the kingside.
